mainTopic: The miracles of the ארון and כרובים, which way the כרובים faced, and a cistern inside a neighbor's house
overview: The גמרא learns from a פסוק that the space under the כרובים' wings was empty, just like the space above them. This supports a tradition from רבי לוי (or רבי יוחנן), backed by a ברייתא, that the ארון and כרובים took up no space in the קודש הקדשים. רבנאי quotes שמואל, who proves from the length of the wings that the כרובים stood בנס (by a miracle). Six אמוראים each push back on that proof by showing a natural way the כרובים could have fit. Next, רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue about which way the כרובים faced, and each side explains the פסוק that seems to go against him. Then a new משנה teaches the rules for someone whose cistern can only be reached through his neighbor's house. The גמרא asks where the locks in the משנה go and why the homeowner needs one. רבי אלעזר's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The space below the wings was empty, like the space above
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that the area under the כרובים' wings was used for nothing, just like the area above them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the verse teaches us: below is like above. Just as the space above was not used for anything, so too the space below was not used for anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining what lesson the פסוק about the כרובים' wings comes to teach. It compares the space under the wings to the empty air above them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The space above the spread wings was obviously empty air. The פסוק teaches that the space below was the same: nothing was there and it served no purpose. This sets up the idea that the כרובים area did not take up usable room.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק about the כרובים' wings that the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: below is like above;
just as above, it is not used for anything,
so too below, it is not used for anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the lesson of the פסוק discussed just before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that the area below the wings, like the area above, was empty and served no function.

steps.title: This supports רבי לוי's tradition that the ארון took no space
steps.stepSummary: The lesson of the פסוק supports רבי לוי (or רבי יוחנן), who had a tradition that the place of the ארון and כרובים is not counted in the measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי לוי, as רבי לוי said (and some say it was רבי יוחנן): We have this as a tradition from our fathers: the place of the ארון and the כרובים is not part of the measurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the idea it just learned matches a known tradition. רבי לוי taught that the ארון and כרובים did not take up any of the room's measured space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the space below the wings was 'used for nothing,' it fits the claim that the ארון and כרובים did not use up floor space. רבי לוי's tradition says this was a miracle passed down, not something he derived himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A tradition in our hands from our fathers
Is not part of the measurement

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous teaching that the ארון miraculously took up no space in the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Levi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Levi said, and some say Rabbi Yoḥanan:
This matter is a tradition in our hands from our fathers:

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם אָרוֹן וּכְרוּבִים אֵינוֹ מִן הַמִּדָּה.
phrases.english: the place of the Ark and the cherubs is not part of the measurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the lesson of step 1 matches an existing tradition.
steps.raayaObject: רבי לוי's tradition that the ארון and כרובים take no space
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק's lesson that the space under the wings was used for nothing

steps.title: A ברייתא: ten אמות of space on every side of the ארון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also teaches that the ארון משה made had ten אמות of open space on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: The ארון that משה made had ten אמות of space on each and every side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same idea as רבי לוי. The ארון had ten אמות of empty space on every side of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קודש הקדשים was twenty אמות wide. If there were ten אמות on each side of the ארון, the two sides already fill all twenty, leaving no room for the ארון itself. So the ארון must have taken up no space at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי לוי's tradition and the ברייתא agree: the ארון and כרובים did not take up any space in the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
The Ark that Moses made
had ten cubits of space
on each and every side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא in support of רבי לוי's tradition.
steps.raayaObject: The ארון took up no physical space
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: ten אמות of space on every side of the ארון

steps.title: שמואל: the כרובים stood by a miracle
steps.stepSummary: רבנאי quotes שמואל that the כרובים stood בנס, and brings a פסוק giving the length of their wings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנאי said in the name of שמואל: The כרובים stood by a miracle, as it says: 'Five אמות was one wing of the כרוב, and five אמות the second wing of the כרוב; ten אמות from the tip of its wings to the tip of its wings.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: שמואל says the כרובים themselves stood miraculously. He starts his proof by quoting the פסוק that gives the wing measurements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each כרוב's wings stretched ten אמות from tip to tip. With two כרובים side by side, the wings alone filled twenty אמות, the whole width of the room. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden winged figures in the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Rabbenai said that Shmuel said:
The cherubs stand by a miracle,
as it says: "And five cubits was one wing of the cherub,
and five cubits was the second wing of the cherub;
ten cubits from the tips of its wings
to the tips of its wings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ארון to a separate miracle about the כרובים themselves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כרובים stood miraculously, without taking up physical space.

steps.title: Where were their bodies? So it must be a miracle
steps.stepSummary: Since the wings filled the whole width, there was no room left for the bodies, so the כרובים must have stood by a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where were their bodies standing? Rather, learn from this: they stand by a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes שמואל's proof. It asks where the bodies could fit and concludes it had to be a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wings came out from the sides of the bodies, so the bodies needed extra room beyond the twenty אמות of wings. But the room was only twenty אמות wide. The only answer is that the כרובים took up no space.

phrases.english: Their bodies, where were they standing?
Rather, learn from this:
they stand by a miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the wing measurements from step 4 to prove the miracle.
steps.raayaObject: The כרובים stood by a miracle
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wings filled all twenty אמות, leaving no room for the bodies

steps.title: אביי: maybe the bodies were under the wings, like chickens
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: maybe the bodies stood beneath the wings, like chickens, so they took no extra space.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: But maybe they stood with bodies sticking out below, like chickens!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges שמואל's proof. He suggests a normal way the bodies could fit without a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wings came out from the middle of the back, like on a chicken, the body would sit under the wings. Then the wings alone measure the full width, and the bodies add no extra room. So the פסוק does not force a miracle.

phrases.english: Abaye objected to it:
But perhaps they stood sticking out, like chickens!
phrases.notes: Picture the wings rising from the back, with the body underneath, so the body adds no width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the פסוק, not necessarily the miracle itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bodies could have been under the wings, needing no extra space

steps.title: רבא: maybe the כרובים were not side by side
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes back: maybe the two כרובים did not stand in line with each other, so the wings overlapped and left room for the bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: But maybe they stood with one not opposite the other!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second way to avoid שמואל's proof. The כרובים may have been arranged so their wings overlapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל assumed the two כרובים stood in a straight line, wing tip to wing tip. If one stood a bit forward or back from the other, their wings could pass each other. That frees up enough room for the bodies.

keyTerms.meaning: One not lined up opposite the other

phrases.english: Rava objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא זֶה שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד זֶה הֲווֹ קָיְימִי!
phrases.english: But perhaps they stood one not opposite the other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate challenge to the proof in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כרובים could have been staggered so the wings overlapped

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: maybe they stood on a diagonal
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב pushes back: maybe the כרובים stood along the diagonal of the room, which is longer than twenty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objected: But maybe they stood on a diagonal!
steps.whatsHappening: A third challenge to שמואל's proof. The כרובים may have been placed corner to corner across the room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A square room's diagonal is longer than its sides. If the כרובים stretched from corner to corner, there would be more than twenty אמות of room. That leaves enough space for both wings and bodies without a miracle.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov objected to it:
But perhaps they stood on a diagonal!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, separate challenge to the proof in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A diagonal placement gives more than twenty אמות of space

steps.title: Maybe the room was wider at the top
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע suggests that the room may have widened higher up, which would leave space for the bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע objects: But perhaps the room widened at the top!
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא attacks the proof that the כרובים needed a miracle. He suggests the room was simply wider up high, where the wings were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that the room's width of twenty אמות was the same all the way up. רב הונא suggests the twenty אמות may describe only the bottom of the room. If the room grew wider higher up, there was extra space, and no miracle was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (he challenges the argument)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua objects to it:
But perhaps the room widened at the top!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth objection in the same series as the objections of אביי, רבא, and רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the proof forces a miracle.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the room had the same width at every height.

steps.title: Maybe the wings were folded
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests the כרובים kept their wings slightly bent, so the wings did not fill the full twenty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: But perhaps they were bending their wings!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another natural way the כרובים could have fit. Maybe their wings were not stretched out all the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof added up the full length of the wings as if they were stretched out flat. If the wings were bent, they took up less than their full length. That leaves room for the bodies.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to it:
But perhaps they were bending their wings!
phrases.notes: The word here literally means 'their hands', but he is talking about the wings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another objection in the same series.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the proof forces a miracle.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the wings were fully stretched out.

steps.title: Maybe the wings crossed over each other
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests the wings overlapped one another, so together they took up less space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: But perhaps the wings were crossing over one another!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the last natural explanation in the list. Maybe the wings overlapped each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wings overlapped, their total length did not stretch across the whole room. That frees up space for the bodies. After all these objections, the proof that a miracle was needed is left unconvincing.

keyTerms.meaning: They were crossing over or overlapping one another

steps.whatToRemember: Six different אמוראים (אביי, רבא, רב אחא בר יעקב, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, רב פפא, and רב אשי) each showed a natural way the כרובים could have fit, so שמואל's proof (quoted by רבנאי) that they stood בנס is not forced.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to it:
But perhaps they were crossing over one another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final objection in the series; it closes the discussion of the miracle.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the proof forces a miracle.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the wings lay side by side with no overlap.

steps.title: Which way did the כרובים face?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the כרובים stood. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue: one says they faced each other, and one says they faced the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: How were they standing? רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree. One says: their faces were toward each other. The other says: their faces were toward the House.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about the כרובים, the direction they faced. It brings a מחלוקת with two opinions, setting up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion matches a different פסוק. One view follows the פסוק that says the כרובים faced each other. The other follows the פסוק that says they faced the House. The גמרא does not tell us which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: Their faces were toward each other
Their faces were toward the House (the היכל)

phrases.english: How were they standing?
Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: פְּנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו,
phrases.english: One says: Their faces were one toward the other,
And one says: Their faces were toward the House.
phrases.notes: 'The House' means the היכל, the main hall outside the קודש הקדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size of the כרובים to the direction they faced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether the כרובים faced each other or faced the היכל.

steps.title: A פסוק says they faced the House
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that the כרובים faced each other, because a פסוק says they faced the House.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says their faces were toward each other, isn't it written: 'And their faces were toward the House'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion with a פסוק that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברי הימים clearly describes the כרובים facing the House. So how can this view hold that they faced each other?

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר פְּנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו,
phrases.english: But according to the one who says their faces were one toward the other,
isn't it written: "And their faces were toward the House"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר פְּנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו הָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first opinion in the מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the כרובים faced each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly says they faced the House.

steps.title: It depended on how the Jewish people behaved
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the כרובים faced each other when the Jewish people did רצון המקום, and faced away when they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Here, the פסוק is speaking of a time when the Jewish people do the will of המקום. There, it is speaking of a time when the Jewish people do not do the will of המקום.
steps.whatsHappening: The first view answers that both פסוקים are true, but at different times. The direction of the כרובים changed with the Jewish people's behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Jewish people did רצון המקום, the כרובים faced each other, like close friends. When they did not, the כרובים turned toward the House. This way, each פסוק describes a different situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source is talking about a different case)

phrases.english: It is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: here, it is when the Jewish people do the will of God,
phrases.notes: 'Here' points to the פסוק that says they faced each other.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: there, it is when the Jewish people do not do the will of God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two פסוקים into two different time periods.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to contradict each other about the direction of the כרובים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The direction changed miraculously, depending on whether the Jewish people did רצון המקום.

steps.title: A פסוק says they faced each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second view, because a פסוק says the כרובים faced each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'and their faces were toward the House,' isn't it written: 'And their faces one toward the other'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the second opinion with the פסוק that supports the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמות says the כרובים faced each other. So how can this view say they faced the House?

keyTerms.meaning: And their faces one toward the other (the פסוק in שמות)

phrases.english: And according to the one who says "And their faces were toward the House,"
isn't it written: "And their faces one toward the other"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר וּפְנֵיהֶם לַבַּיִת הָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 13, this time attacking the second opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the כרובים faced the House.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly says they faced each other.

steps.title: They were turned partly sideways
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the כרובים were angled to the side, so they faced both each other and the House at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were angled sideways.
steps.whatsHappening: The second view answers that the כרובים stood at an angle, so both פסוקים are describing the same position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not split the פסוקים into different times. Instead, a slanted position lets both descriptions be true at the same moment: partly toward each other, and partly toward the House.

keyTerms.meaning: They were turned to the side (at an angle)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is different from the one in step 14. There, the direction changed over time. Here, a single angled position fits both פסוקים at once.

phrases.english: They were angled sideways –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciles both פסוקים with one angled position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Facing the House and facing each other seem to be two directions that cannot both be true.
steps.terutzMaskana: An angled stance makes both descriptions true at once.

steps.title: אונקלוס הגר: like a student leaving his teacher
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from אונקלוס הגר supports the answer: the כרובים had the form of children, and their faces were turned sideways like a student taking leave of his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: אונקלוס הגר said: The כרובים are 'the work of children's form,' and their faces were turned to the side, like a student taking leave of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the idea that the כרובים stood at an angle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student leaving his teacher does not turn his back completely. He turns partly away while still facing his teacher a little. אונקלוס says the כרובים were angled the same way, which backs up the answer in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of children's form (shaped like children)
Like a student taking leave of his teacher

steps.whatToRemember: One view: the כרובים faced each other or turned away, depending on the Jewish people's behavior. The other view: they stood at an angle, like a student leaving his teacher.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Onkelos the convert said:
The cherubs are "the work of children's form,"
and their faces are turned sideways
like a student taking leave of his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a source for the answer in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the כרובים stood at an angle.

steps.title: משנה: a cistern inside a neighbor's house
steps.stepSummary: Someone who owns a cistern reachable only through another person's house may enter only at normal hours, may not bring his animal inside, and each side may install a lock.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone whose cistern is inside his friend's house may enter at a time when people usually enter, and leave at a time when people usually leave. He may not bring his animal in to drink from his cistern. Instead, he fills water and gives it to the animal outside. And this one makes himself a lock, and that one makes himself a lock.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new topic. It sets the rules for a man who must pass through his neighbor's house to reach his own cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He has a right to reach his cistern, but he must not be a burden on the homeowner. So he comes only at normal hours and keeps his animal outside. Each side may also install a lock; the גמרא will ask why the homeowner would need one.
steps.whatToRemember: The cistern owner may use his access, but in a way that bothers the homeowner as little as possible, and both sides may put on locks.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who has a cistern
beyond the house of his friend –

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנָס בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם נִכְנָסִין,
phrases.english: enters at a time when people usually enter,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹצֵא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹצְאִין.
phrases.english: and leaves at a time when people usually leave.
And he may not bring in his animal and water it from his cistern,
rather, he fills water and gives it to the animal outside.
And this one makes himself a lock,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the cistern owner, who can lock his cistern.

phrases.english: and that one makes himself a lock.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the homeowner, who may also put on a lock.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בּוֹר לִפְנִים מִבֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, unrelated to the כרובים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cistern owner enters and leaves only at normal hours, waters his animal outside, and both he and the homeowner may install locks.

steps.title: Where does the lock go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where the lock mentioned in the משנה is placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A lock on what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking a simple question. The משנה said each side may put on a lock, but it did not say what the lock is on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible places for a lock: the door of the house or the cistern itself. The גמרא wants to know which one the משנה means before it can understand the rule.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A lock to where?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the end of step 18, where each side may put on a lock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the lock is on the house or on the cistern.

steps.title: Both locks go on the cistern
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that both the cistern owner and the homeowner put their locks on the cistern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them put a lock on the cistern.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. Both people lock the cistern, so neither one can use it without the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because there are two locks on the cistern, the cistern can only be opened when both people are there. This keeps either side from going to the cistern alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern, a pit that holds water

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Both of them, to the cistern.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both locks are placed on the cistern.

steps.title: Why would the homeowner lock the cistern?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why the cistern owner wants a lock, but asks why the homeowner would need one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the cistern owner wants a lock, because he wants to protect the water in his cistern. But why does the homeowner need one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. The cistern owner has a clear reason for a lock, but the homeowner seems to have no reason to lock a cistern that is not his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cistern owner wants to stop the homeowner from taking his water. The homeowner owns none of the water, so the גמרא asks what he gains by locking the cistern.

phrases.english: Granted, the owner of the cistern:
he wants to protect the water of his cistern;
but the homeowner, why does he need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the homeowner also locks the cistern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The homeowner has no water to protect, so a lock on the cistern seems useless to him.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר begins to answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר starts to explain why the homeowner needs a lock. His answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the answer to the question of step 21. Only the name of the one answering appears here, and his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר is about to give the homeowner a reason to lock the cistern. Keep the question in mind: what does the homeowner gain from a lock on a cistern that is not his?

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: His actual answer comes right after this, on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup only; the answer continues in the next part of the text.
